services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenTelemetry Collector - Central telemetry receiver and router
  # ==========================================================================
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.115.1
    container_name: otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver
      - "8888:8888"   # Prometheus metrics (collector self-metrics)
      - "8889:8889"   # Prometheus exporter (for scraped metrics)
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:13133/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3001 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================

    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}

      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f autokuma || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.11.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord

    container_name: immich_server

    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    env_file:
      - .env
    ports:
      - 2283:2283
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - database
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '4.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  immich-machine-learning:
    container_name: immich_machine_learning
    # Using CPU image since AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) needs ROCm 6.4.4+
    # Immich ROCm image only has 6.3.4
    # Change to :release-rocm if/when Immich updates ROCm version
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}

    volumes:

          cpus: '4.0'

    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  redis:
    container_name: immich_redis
    image: docker.io/valkey/valkey:8-bookworm

      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:

          cpus: '0.5'

      test: valkey-cli ping || exit 1
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:

        --tuples-only --no-align --command='SELECT COALESCE(SUM(googlechecksum(googlechecksum(tableoid,
        entity_id))), 0) FROM entity WHERE NOT is_external')"; Prev="$$(cat
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum 2>/dev/null || echo '')"; echo "$${Chksum}" >
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum; test "$${Prev}" = '' -o "$${Prev}" = "$${Chksum}"

        '-c',
        'search_path="$$user", public, vectors',

  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)

    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.5
    environment:

# Following TRaSH Guides best practices

name: media-management

networks:
  media-net:
    driver: bridge

  # ==========================================================================
  # Gluetun - VPN Gateway (NordVPN WireGuard)
  # ==========================================================================
  gluetun:
    image: qmcgaw/gluetun:v3.40.3
    container_name: gluetun
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    networks:
      - media-net
    environment:
      - VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER=nordvpn
      - VPN_TYPE=wireguard
      - WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY=${NORDVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY}
      - SERVER_COUNTRIES=Netherlands
      - TZ=America/New_York
      # Allow access to container network for inter-service communication
      - FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS=192.168.1.0/24
      # Health check settings
      - HEALTH_VPN_DURATION_INITIAL=30s
      - HEALTH_VPN_DURATION_ADDITION=10s
    ports:
      # qBittorrent
      - "8080:8080"
      - "6881:6881"
      - "6881:6881/udp"
      # SABnzbd
      - "8085:8085"
      # Prowlarr
      - "9696:9696"
      # FlareSolverr
      - "8191:8191"
    volumes:
      - gluetun-data:/gluetun
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- ifconfig.me || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # qBittorrent - BitTorrent Client (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  qbittorrent:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:5.1.4
    container_name: qbittorrent
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - WEBUI_PORT=8080
    volumes:
      - qbittorrent-config:/config
      - /data/torrents:/data/torrents
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prowlarr - Indexer Manager (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  prowlarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:2.3.0
    container_name: prowlarr
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - prowlarr-config:/config
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9696/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

    image: ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:v3.4.6

    environment:
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
      - LOG_HTML=false
      - CAPTCHA_SOLVER=none

    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8191/health || exit 1"]

## Grafana Docker Resource Recommendations

### General Hardware Guidelines

For Grafana Enterprise products, the recommended ratio is 1:4 CPU to memory (1 CPU core for every 4GB of memory), with deployment on machines having 16 CPU cores and 64GB of memory.(no content)Similarly, Grafana Enterprise Traces recommends 4GB of memory for every CPU core, with at least 16 CPU cores and 64GB of memory.

### Container Memory Considerations

When Grafana runs in a container (Docker or Kubernetes), it doesn't have access to full system memory, and if Grafana crosses container limits, it can get killed even if the host system has RAM to spare.(no content)For small teams with 5-10 users and basic dashboards, expect 200-500MB of memory usage, which includes the base Grafana process plus typical dashboard caching.

## AMD GPU Hardware Transcoding in Jellyfin Docker

### Memory Requirements
For most configurations, at least 8GB of RAM is recommended, though for a Linux server running without a GUI, 4GB should be enough.

### Docker Configuration
The official Jellyfin Docker image supports all major acceleration methods including VA-API, and you need to pass in your GPU devices and grant the container permission to use them by mapping `/dev/dri` devices and using `group_add: render`.

### AMD GPU Support & Limitations
AMD Graphics have poor encoder quality and poor driver support, even on Linux. However, VA-API is preferred on all AMD GPUs with full acceleration on Polaris (RX400/500)+ GPUs and is open source, while AMF is not recommended with limited support.

### Codec Support
AMD supports AV1 decoding on Radeon RX 6000 series and newer (except RX 6400/6500), and AV1 encoding on Radeon RX 7000 series and newer.

The documentation recommends using VA-API for AMD GPUs in Docker with proper device mapping and group permissions for optimal hardware transcoding performance.

## AMD GPU Support with ROCm

Ollama supports AMD GPUs through the ROCm library, with support for Radeon RX 7900-6800 series, Vega 64, Radeon PRO W7900-W6800 series, and Instinct MI300-MI60 series.

## Docker Deployment

For running Ollama with AMD GPUs in Docker:

**Basic ROCm-supported GPUs:**
If you have an AMD GPU that supports ROCm, you can run the ROCm version using `docker run -d --restart always --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama:rocm`

**Unsupported AMD GPUs (with workaround):**
For GPUs like the Radeon 6700 XT, you can use `docker run -d --restart always --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama -e HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0 -e HCC_AMDGPU_TARGET=gfx1030 ollama/ollama:rocm`

## Memory & CPU Recommendations

**Memory Requirements:**
- Ollama's memory requirements scale with model size, and when using GPU acceleration, system RAM requirements are reduced as model layers are offloaded to GPU VRAM
- For most users, 8-12GB VRAM is the sweet spot, allowing you to run 7-8B parameter models like Llama 3.1 8B with Q4_K_M quantization at 40+ tokens/second

**Hardware Recommendations by Budget:**

*Budget Setup:*
A modern 6-core CPU from Intel or AMD, 16GB of DDR4 RAM, and a GPU with at least 8GB of VRAM

*Mid-Range:*
A recent 8-core CPU, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and an AMD RX 7800 XT (16GB)

*High-End:*
A high-end CPU like AMD Ryzen 9, and 64GB or more of DDR5 RAM

## Configuration Optimization

For AMD GPUs, install ROCm support and set AMD GPU variables: `export HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0` and `export OLLAMA_GPU_DRIVER=rocm`(no content)Strategic resource allocation across CPU, GPU, and memory systems can deliver performance gains of 300-500% over default settings

Based on the search results, here are the best practices for PostgreSQL Docker memory and CPU resource limits in 2025:

## Memory Limits

Use the `--memory` and `--cpus` flags to allocate appropriate resources to the PostgreSQL container, ensuring it has enough memory and CPU resources to handle the workload without causing resource contention.

A common configuration limits the container to using 2GB of RAM and around 1.5 CPU cores, balancing performance and resource consumption. Limiting a PostgreSQL container to 2GB of RAM ensures it doesn't starve other applications.

### Shared Memory Considerations

Docker containers have an artificial limit placed on shared memory space, with a default limit of 64MB. When using Docker Compose, set shared memory limit with `shm_size: 128mb` to avoid PostgreSQL shared memory issues.

## CPU Limits

Set resource limits on your PostgreSQL container to prevent it from consuming excessive host resources using the `--memory` and `--cpus` flags. You can specify CPU limits as a number of CPU cores (e.g., `--cpus="1.5"`) or use CPU shares for relative allocation.

## Implementation Methods

**Docker Run Command:**
```bash
docker run --memory="2g" --cpus="1.5" --shm-size="128mb" postgres
```

**Docker Compose:**
Create deploy and resources segments in your service configuration with limits for CPUs and memory, plus reservations for minimum guaranteed resources.

## Monitoring

The `docker stats` command provides a live stream of resource usage statistics, displaying CPU percentage and current memory usage versus the configured memory limit. Observing docker stats can reveal containers that are frequently hitting their CPU or memory limits, indicating a need to increase these limits or optimize the application itself.

## Additional Best Practices

- Include a health check using pg_isready command, running every 30 seconds to allow Docker to confirm your database remains operational and responsive
- Use dedicated volumes for data storage to improve I/O performance
- Keep container images up to date for security patches and performance improvements
- Consider using Alpine-based images for lighter deployments with reduced memory footprint

## Docker Configuration Recommendations

### CPU Limits

For optimal performance, pin Redis/Valkey to specific CPU cores using the `--cpuset-cpus` Docker flag, which reduces cross-core contention and improves cache locality, critical for minimizing tail latencies at high throughput.

Example configuration from benchmarks:
Docker run command using `--cpuset-cpus="2-7"` with `--io-threads 6` for a configuration with multiple cores

**Thread Recommendations:**
Valkey recommends setting the number of threads to be a value less than the number of cores you have to avoid CPU over-subscription, which can degrade performance.

### Memory Limits

**Setting Memory Limits:**
In production benchmarks, a `--maxmemory 10gb` limit was used to prevent unbounded memory growth.

**Why Memory Limits Matter:**
Running Redis with unlimited memory (maxmemory = 0) causes problems after a few days as the system runs out of RAM and Redis enters a restart loop

**Best Practice:**
Setting a memory limit makes Redis return an out-of-memory error for write commands when it reaches the limit, preventing the whole machine from dying due to memory starvation

### Monitoring Thresholds

Set CPU threshold at 90% of available CPU, but because Valkey and Redis are single-threaded, the actual threshold should be calculated as a fraction of the node's total capacity

### Connection Limits

Valkey nodes can have up to either 10,000 simultaneous connections or 4 simultaneous connections per megabyte of memory, whichever is larger

### 2025 Performance Updates

Valkey 8.1 introduced up to 20% memory efficiency improvements by rebuilding its key-value store based on modern data structures similar to Google's "Swiss Tables"

## Memory Recommendations

Users have reported running qBittorrent in Docker containers with 4GB memory limits, though the appropriate amount depends heavily on your workload:

- **For typical use (100-1000 torrents)**: With 89 torrents, users report needing around 4GB
- **For heavy use**: One user with 1,200 torrents reported using 21 GiB of RAM, while another with 40k torrents on Windows used only 2.5 GiB, suggesting Docker containers may use more memory than native installations
- **Very large libraries**: With 1,000 active torrents, users reported qBittorrent consuming 16+ GB of memory

**Important considerations:**
- The disk cache uses more RAM than configured, typically 20-50% more (e.g., 15 GB cache may use 18 GB RAM)
- If you limit RAM too restrictively, it will eventually crash the container

## CPU Recommendations

CPU usage varies significantly based on activity and configuration:

- Seeding 600+ torrents can cause 40% CPU usage, with downloading pushing it to 90-100%
- Some users experience 100% CPU consumption in Docker containers, often related to specific configurations
- Normal operation with 15 active downloads shouldn't exceed 40% CPU

**CPU issues can be caused by:**
- Large numbers of torrents with queueing enabled
- VPN overhead
- High connection counts

## General Recommendations

For a balanced Docker deployment:
- **Memory**: Start with 2-4GB for light use, 8-12GB for moderate use (hundreds of torrents), and monitor usage
- **CPU**: Generally doesn't need hard limits unless you're experiencing issues, but be aware that high torrent counts or certain configurations can cause spikes
- Monitor actual usage and adjust based on your specific torrent count and activity level

Based on my review of your docker-compose files and comparison with official documentation and community best practices, here's a comprehensive analysis of the resource limits for your major services:

### 1. Prometheus (Current: 4096m / 2.0 CPUs)

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml`

**Official Recommendation:** No specific resource limits in official documentation

**Analysis:** 
- Prometheus has no built-in memory limiting and uses what it needs based on metrics collected
- A rule of thumb: total memory / 10,000 = max memory series (e.g., 64GB = ~6M series)
- Your 4GB limit is reasonable for a homelab with moderate metric ingestion

**Verdict:** GOOD - Appropriate for homelab scale

**Sources:**
- [Prometheus Issue #1836](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/1836)
- [Prometheus Users Group](https://groups.google.com/g/prometheus-users/c/K-63dBkJwuY)

### 2. Grafana (Current: 4096m / 2.0 CPUs)

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml`

**Official Recommendation:** 200-500MB for small teams (5-10 users)

**Analysis:**
- For small teams with basic dashboards, typical usage is 200-500MB
- Grafana Enterprise products recommend 1:4 CPU to memory ratio (1 CPU : 4GB RAM)
- Your 4GB allocation is generous for a homelab
- Best practice: memory requests = limits (you follow this with reservations)

**Verdict:** OVER-PROVISIONED - Could reduce to 1024-2048m safely

**Justification for Current Values:** If you're running many complex dashboards with heavy queries, the higher allocation provides headroom. However, monitoring actual usage would likely show 1-2GB is sufficient.

**Sources:**
- [Grafana Hardware Requirements Community Discussion](https://community.grafana.com/t/hardware-requirements-for-a-grafana-server/2853)
- [Grafana Memory Management](https://last9.io/blog/grafana-memory-usage/)
- [GEM Hardware Requirements](https://grafana.com/docs/enterprise-metrics/latest/set-up/hardware/)

### 3. Ollama (Current: 4096m / 4.0 CPUs)

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/docker-compose.yml`

**Official Recommendation:** No hard limits, but 8-12GB VRAM + 16-32GB RAM recommended for mid-range setups

**Analysis:**
- You're using ROCm with AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150)
- For 7-8B parameter models, typical requirements: 8-12GB VRAM + system RAM
- Memory requirements scale with model size; GPU offloading reduces system RAM needs
- 4GB system memory limit may be too restrictive when running larger models
- CPU limit of 4.0 is good for parallel processing

**Verdict:** UNDER-PROVISIONED (Memory) - Consider increasing to 8192m or removing limit

**Justification:** With GPU acceleration, most model inference happens on GPU VRAM, but initial loading and some operations still need system RAM. 8GB would be safer.

**Sources:**
- [Ollama Hardware Guide](https://www.arsturn.com/blog/ollama-hardware-guide-what-you-need-to-run-llms-locally)
- [Ollama VRAM Requirements 2025](https://localllm.in/blog/ollama-vram-requirements-for-local-llms)

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/immich/deploy/docker-compose.yml`

**Official Recommendation:** 
- Minimum: 4GB RAM, 2 CPU cores
- Recommended: 6GB RAM, 4 CPU cores

**Analysis:**
- Your immich-server: 4096m / 4.0 CPUs ✓ (meets minimum, below recommended)
- Your immich-machine-learning: 4096m / 4.0 CPUs ✓ (reasonable, CPU-based ML)
- Your immich_postgres: 1024m / 2.0 CPUs ⚠️ (below 2GB recommendation)
- Your immich_redis: 512m / 1.0 CPUs ✓ (adequate for caching)

**Verdict:** 
- **Immich services:** GOOD (at minimum spec)
- **PostgreSQL:** UNDER-PROVISIONED - Should be 2048m minimum

**Justification:** The official docs specifically state PostgreSQL needs at least 2GB when using Docker limits. Your 1GB allocation could cause issues during bulk imports or ML processing.

**Sources:**

- [Immich GitHub Discussion #4364](https://github.com/immich-app/immich/discussions/4364)
- [Docker-compose resource limits discussion](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1325830976495943750)

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/jellyfin/deploy/docker-compose.yml`

**Official Recommendation:** 8GB RAM minimum (4GB for headless Linux), 4+ threads when using hardware acceleration

**Analysis:**
- You're using AMD GPU hardware transcoding (VA-API)
- Official docs recommend 8GB RAM for most configurations
- 4GB might work for headless Linux without GUI
- With AMD Radeon for transcoding, any modern 4-thread CPU handles the workload well
- Your CPU allocation of 4.0 cores is excellent for transcoding

**Verdict:** UNDER-PROVISIONED (Memory) - Consider increasing to 8192m

**Justification:** While 4GB might work, official recommendations are 8GB. Hardware transcoding with VA-API reduces CPU load but memory usage for large libraries and concurrent streams benefits from more RAM.

**Sources:**
- [Jellyfin Hardware Selection](https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/administration/hardware-selection/)

### 6. PostgreSQL Instances (Current: 1024m / 1.0-2.0 CPUs)

**Files:** Multiple (Jellystat, Paperless, Immich databases)

**Official Recommendation:** 2GB typical, requires shm_size configuration

**Analysis:**
- Your limits: Generally 1024m across all PostgreSQL instances
- Best practice: 2GB for production workloads
- Critical: Docker containers have 64MB default shared memory limit
- PostgreSQL needs shm_size configured (recommended: 128mb-256mb)

**Current Configs:**
- `jellystat-db`: 1024m / 1.0 CPUs (no shm_size) ⚠️
- `paperless-db`: 1024m / 1.0 CPUs (no shm_size) ⚠️
- `immich_postgres`: 1024m / 2.0 CPUs (no shm_size) ⚠️

**Verdict:** UNDER-PROVISIONED - Missing shm_size configuration

**Recommended Changes:**
```yaml
deploy:

    limits:
      memory: 2048m
      cpus: '1.5'
shm_size: 128mb  # Add this at service level
```

**Sources:**

- Your 512m allocation is reasonable for caching use cases
- Important: Need to set `maxmemory` parameter in Redis config to prevent unlimited growth
